head: 9cfe8339823775fcbf38719b342f1407864c03d6
summary: Fail. This head adds a careful, fail-closed draft of guarded post-merge issue closure, plus the read-only request_history.py and its controls. It does not deliver the outcome issue #115 asks for. recovery_entry.verify_rollout still always raises recovery_rollout_not_verified, and every guarded path calls it first: the recovery entry, the guarded native writer, adoption_guard.begin and the target-review preflight. No recovery workflow is deployed. The unguarded writer prints AW_POST_MERGE_CHECKPOINT_V1 records, but nothing consumes them. As a result, a linked issue still stays open after an asynchronous native merge unless a human closes it, which is what happened with Core #75, #77 and #79. There is no hosted asynchronous merge-and-close proof; the Core #77 fixture records a manual close. The controlled hosted issues:write comparison was not performed. Several gaps the human listed remain open: actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and cancellation, and recovery before the first status. The queued-PR liveness bug from the previous review is unchanged at this head (native_merge.reconcile, block_unadmitted). request_history is explicitly observation-only and does not fix it. Hosted controls passed 832 synthetic tests (current-head CI succeeded), but that does not substitute for hosted closure proof or for rollout.

findings.title: Verified issue closure is never reachable
findings.detail: verify_rollout always raises recovery_rollout_not_verified, and every guarded entry point calls it before any write. No recovery workflow is deployed, and nothing consumes the AW_POST_MERGE_CHECKPOINT_V1 records the unguarded writer emits. After an asynchronous native merge, the linked issue still stays open until a human closes it.
findings.required_fix: Implement and review a rollout evidence verifier. Deploy the recovery workflow through the reviewed policy-adoption path. Demonstrate automatic closure.

findings.title: Queued PR can be blocked indefinitely by block_unadmitted under its own retained guard
findings.detail: After run A queues a PR, settle and cancel_blocked retain A's merge guard while the request exists. On any later wake, guarded.begin fails for that PR. block_unadmitted then sees the newest Actions status is success and posts pending. No later run can acquire the guard to re-verify and publish success, and the request is never cancelled. The strict required status therefore blocks the merge. request_history.py at this head is observation-only and explicitly does not restore the status.
findings.required_fix: Let the owner of the queued guard re-verify and re-publish success, or bind request provenance to the guard so a later run can safely take over or cancel. Add a control for a queued PR followed by a later wake.

findings.title: No real hosted asynchronous merge and automatic close proof
findings.detail: The issue requires verifying actual cloud behavior before claiming automatic closure. The only real-provider evidence is the Core #77 fixture, which shows a manual close.
findings.required_fix: Run and record a controlled hosted asynchronous native merge in which the mechanism closes the linked issue. Include hosted negative controls.

findings.title: issues:write permission hypothesis not tested
findings.detail: The issue requires a controlled hosted comparison before changing a production permission or treating native auto-close as reliable. No comparison is recorded.
findings.required_fix: Perform and document the controlled hosted comparison. Keep the exact CI, independent review and ownership gates.

findings.title: Actor and launcher adoption, request ownership and pre-status recovery remain unimplemented
findings.detail: cancel_blocked always retains a queued request because its provenance cannot be bound to a run. Cancellation and its race with merging are unimplemented. An admission interrupted before the first status has no durable recovery for the pending write. rollout_inventory cannot prove that launchers have stopped, and request_history cannot prove who authored a request.
findings.required_fix: Bind native request provenance to the guard. Implement safe cancellation and recovery for crashes before the first status. Provide verified evidence of actor and launcher adoption.
